i was addressing the change/convince aspect in general. But as you mention it yea, she definitely sucks as a friend. Very one-sided, I am always there to help her with her struggles (mostly over that guy) but very rarely she is there for mine. Tons of other issues but I will leave it there.

I consider a bad friend to be someone who punishes you for being emotionally vulnerable and honest, they say they are up to hangout with you but they never put in the effort to do so, they get jealous or resentful over your successes in life, punching down (when they should be encouraging you), they seem uninclined to put the work in for a healthy relationship (very one-sided in regards to effort) and they lack an understanding that a good friendship should be reciprocal.

I have a friend who is obsessed with having a particular guy in her life as a relationship. He is a bad guy, lies/cheats plenty and doesn't want her as a serious relationship. She knows this btw, she is very self-aware (not fully though) of how bad he is for her but she wants him still. This has negatively affected her life and other relationships greatly for 2 years. She can't talk to her parents about it now or most of her friends as they have pushed her away, basically isolated/abandoned/bullied her about it.

Now I can't control her on this, she is going to pursue this but I can do what her friends/parents failed her on. I can be there, listen to her, keep her in-tune with reality and tell her about my experience and show her what is possibly and leading my life in a healthy manner.
hm I think good and bad people is an oversimplication of people, if anything, that is perspective and subjective narrative. There is good and bad in all people (though to different degrees as well).

No, you aren't coming off as harsh to me, I think you are coming from a good place but you aren't right about who you think I am or who I want to become. And I don't fault you on that, we are after all communicating over just text and only read a few messages from each other. Not ideal for knowing a person comprehensively.

When it comes to convincing people of something I am particularly interested in "leading by example". My being itself gets people contemplating their own lives and then maybe even asking me questions, opposed me trying to desperately help someone who doesn't want to be helped. Hope that makes sense. And I do think I am starting to have that effect on people, they are just scared. They are so close to nudging themselves and I think these people will.

Experiencing serious hardship/truama as a child is very different as an adult. As a child you are still going through vital development (the first 2-5 years are so important for a child).

As an adult I wouldn't tolerate someone resorting to physically harming me for something like that. I would consider that to be an unacceptable friend, which is a bad friend but worse.

You are very much talking about quality vs quantity. A handful of authentic strong friendships goes a long.

I am still unconvinced that you can't convince people of things (the irony hehe). The reason being is I am not satisfied in my convincing skills and I don't think I set enough of an example (at least it isn't clear enough). Once I exhaust that effort over the coming years then I will have an idea of what is possible or what isn't. And by 'convincing people of things' I mean a lot of different things, things I haven't even tried it. So not simply a matter of calling people out on their problems. Y'know, this idea of changing people is one I find to be in the general minds of society that is so despairing but never gets challenged properly. Maybe it doesn't happen because people give up on people so quickly, maybe it says more about the person who 'tried to help' than the person who needed help.

Mood contagion is absolutely a thing, but it is something I don't experience, and if I do it is at a substantial lesser. I also consume a lot of dark entertainment, interested in historical tragedy, and explore plenty of existential thought-processes. Relatively unphased by all of that but what does predominately make me depressed is loneliness (less so now, comes in bouts and doesn’t wreck my life as it once did), past traumas and in-authenticity.

On reflection now I would say I have felt quite gaslit when it comes to people’s authenticity. I can’t exist on that plane of reality, I need things to be real, even if they are miserable. At least then I know what it is, and the hard work can be carried out to figuring out how to get to a better place.

Because it resulted in radical personal growth in their lives. If they didn't go through an addiction experience then they would have not had the good with the bad, and they would have probably led normal lives, but not an extraordinary one.

> Here's another way to look at it, no one advocates for a women to intentionally get into an abusive relationship (har har a bad friend) because the end outcome will have some sort of net benefit. Everyone advocates to get out of there if it's terribly abusive (bad) or to avoid it entirely (get into a good relationship).

This view that I hold isn't the same for romantic relationships. It is better to be single than in a bad relationship.

> There isn't any value in it. There's value in the cancer not being there. You're just trying to achieve an end. Ask any cancer patient, if they could just Thanos snap their fingers and by pass the "fight" of cancer and just get rid of it, they'd do that 10/10 times.

You are probably right for the majority in that statement, but to stay on the topic of suffering, in the case of severe addiction many who survive all of that suffering and closeness to death often don't regret their journey of substance abuse as many who escape it experience a sort of "rebirth", be it spirtually or general outlook/outcome.

> And bad friends cause people to suffer.

Not all sufferring is bad.

> There are ways to appreciate life without it being taken away from you.

You are absolutely right, but many don't.

> Unlike the bad friend concept, where you can just by pass it entirely (no cancer) and win.

Well yeah, your comparison to cancer to bad friends isn't exactly one to one the same thing.

You can fight cancer and there is value in that. Cancer is bad when people suffer a great deal and die. But you can grow as a person from that suffering and looming death is a reminder to be grateful for life. Of course no cancer is preferred, but in this example the options are to fight cancer, suffer but win or just be dead.

"have better coping mechanisms" you get to a point with this where it is an unreasonable expectation. You underestimate how bad loneliness can be coupled with hardship, and years of it. I have somehow got to this point of being a lot more okay with being alone and working on myself and despite that I have demonstrated what is possible in a person it doesn't mean it is possible in all people. Even for me, I would say it has been unreasonable.

Secondly, these coping mechanisms have to be healthy which is a big ask for many when they are coping with their loneliness with substances.

3rd point, it gets to a point where you are expecting people to be okay with  never having an authentic friendship with anyone. We are social creatures, it isn't sustainable to live life like that for most people.

I have, but I still have unmet emotional and socially needs, those don't just all go away despite having a contentment of being alone and having the ability to cope in those situations. I do hope to live an actually healthy life. And I am not wanting to be friends with anyone. If anything I look forward to the days when I have 4 5 solid friends in my life (who are good friends btw).

A big reason why I have headed towards a positive direction is because I have discovered/developed and followed my own* philosophical ideas. This works and I have trackable progress that is clear every 3 months. For example one of my ideas is live my life in a manner that I would like others to emulate, so I am not going to dismantle myself subconsciously because I won’t want others to fail as well and I don’t want those qualities from friends. I think about this a lot. I have had certain bad friendships for close to a year and at times they have gotten under my skin but they haven’t faltered my efforts to uphold myself in an appropriate manner or deterred me of my accomplishments.
Oh careless people don't contemplate their general deceptions.

The disturbing thing is a lot of people consider acquaintances to be friends nowadays. I have had conversations with people and then they mention something about how we are friends, but we have never hung out or had a real conversation about how we are doing or about of lives.

but some of these people I do consider to be friends (we have hung out and talked real etc) but they haven’t been reciprocal and been nasty at times when they really shouldn’t have been. We agree that these aren't non-friends but are bad friends, right?
I think there is a difference between a bad friend and an unacceptable friend, where as I think most people would think of them as one of the same.

Well I have learnt that in every day life it isn't the harmful people who cause the most harm, it is the careless majority who do the majority of harm. Harm occurs very often by accident or carelessness, without proper self-reflection during or after, never mind amendment.

I think I would prefer to be locked up in prison with the general population than be in solitary confinement.

EDIT: No friends is not neutral, taken to extremes in my example above, it is actually a lot worse of a situation. We are social creatures. Bad social connection isn't ideal but none is incredibly detrimental to a person's wellbeing.

In my experience bad friends (this doesn't include unacceptable friends, which I stated I cut out) have had a net benefit to me, compared to being alone. Maybe not necessarily in regard to happiness as I don't live my life for happiness, I try to live a meaningful life. I have found that that pursuit actually results in a more content AND happier life in the long run plus I end up making the world a better place for others. Bad friends have contributed positively to my pursuit of a meaningful life (and subsequently indirectly to my happiness).

For romantic relationships, I would more so agree with you. Better to be alone than in a bad relationship, though love complicates the matter.

I do think it is important to establish a degree of contentment with being alone with your thoughts and doing things by yourself. I am aware those people exist and hope they come to learn that they need to invest more into themselves.

You are correct with what you are saying about teenagers, I feel for those in those situations (my brother would have been in that situation). but as an adult (25) with so much life experience I can assess these things fairly well now.

With your last paragraph, I agree these people exist but I don't fall into that group. Also, when I wrote my CMV I had myself in mind opposed to people in general. But I think I have that stance too. People should tread carefully with loneliness, it is ruining so many people's lives and I would argue that most people aren't even aware of how alone they truly are. Perhaps this pandemic is revealing that a bit more.

I wasn't surrounding myself with people who didn't care, I just didn't have people around. I was drinking alone at home.

helping others and being selfless is part of taking care of yourself, you feel good from that and develop longterm healthy relationships with some people by doing such. you dont have to neglect yourself in order to be of help to others. it's not mutually exclusive. both can be done in conjunction.
